title: Medicare Card Scam Calls
how_it_works: Scammers call pretending to be from Medicare, saying you need a new card or your benefits will stop. They ask for your Medicare number or other personal information.
example_message: "This is Medicare calling. We need to send you a new card. Please confirm your Medicare number and address."
red_flags: Unsolicited call about your Medicare card
Asked to give your Medicare or Social Security number
Threatens to stop your benefits if you don't respond
what_to_do: Hang up and call Medicare directly at 1-800-MEDICARE if you have questions.

title: Fake Package Delivery Texts
how_it_works: You get a text saying a package couldn't be delivered and you need to click a link to reschedule or pay a fee. The link leads to a fake website that tries to steal your information or money.
example_message: "Your package is waiting for delivery. Please click here to reschedule: [fake link]"
red_flags: Link to a website you don't recognize
Requests for payment or personal details
what_to_do: Do not click the link. Delete the text and contact the delivery company using their official website or phone number.

title: Social Security Email Phishing
how_it_works: Scammers send emails pretending to be from Social Security, claiming there's a problem with your account. They ask you to click a link or call a number to fix it, but it's a trick to steal your information.
example_message: "We have detected suspicious activity on your Social Security account. Click here to verify your information."
red_flags: Email says there's a problem with your Social Security
Asks you to click a link or download an attachment
what_to_do: Do not click any links or give out information. Go to the official Social Security website or call them directly.

title: Facebook Marketplace Rental Scam
how_it_works: Scammers post fake rental listings on Facebook Marketplace. They ask for a deposit or rent up front, but there is no real property to rent.
example_message: "This beautiful apartment is available now! Send a deposit to hold it and I'll mail you the keys."
red_flags: Deal seems too good to be true
Asked to send money before seeing the place
Landlord refuses to meet in person
what_to_do: Never send money for a rental you haven't seen in person and always meet the landlord before paying.

title: Grandparent Emergency Scam
how_it_works: Someone calls pretending to be your grandchild or a lawyer, saying your grandchild is in trouble and needs money right away. They ask you to send cash or gift cards.
example_message: "Grandma, I’m in jail and need money for bail. Please don’t tell mom and dad. Can you send $2,000 right away?"
red_flags: Caller wants you to keep it a secret
Requests payment by wire transfer or gift cards
what_to_do: Hang up and call your grandchild or another family member to check if the story is true.
